title: Why you suddenly feel watched, even when alone
hook: Why do you feel watched, even when nobody is there?

narration.text: That feeling of being watched, even in an empty room, is your brain's threat detection system.
Your brain constantly scans for potential dangers, even in your peripheral vision.
It can misinterpret subtle cues, like shadows or patterns, as a hidden presence.
This ancient survival mechanism prioritises safety over perfect accuracy.
It is better to be alert to a false alarm than miss a real threat.
So, that eerie feeling is just your brain doing its job, keeping you safe.
Tell us in the comments if this feeling surprised you, like this video, and subscribe for more insights into your mind.

description: Have you ever felt a strange presence when you were completely alone? It might not be what you think. This Short explains the surprising reason behind that eerie feeling, rooted in your brain's ancient survival instincts.
topic: Why you suddenly feel watched, even when no one is there. This is your brain's threat detection system at work.
